items.title: Cabazitaxel, Carboplatin, Cetrelimab, and Niraparib for Aggressive Variant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a combination treatment for aggressive variant metastatic prostate cancer. Patients receive chemotherapy (cabazitaxel and carboplatin) plus immunotherapy (cetrelimab), followed by a PARP inhibitor (niraparib) with or without continued immunotherapy. The study is no longer enrolling new patients but continues to follow participants already enrolled.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Study of AZD0516 in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-stage trial evaluates the safety and tolerability of AZD0516, a new investigational drug, either alone or combined with other anti-cancer treatments for metastatic prostate cancer. The study is actively recruiting patients. AZD0516 represents a novel therapeutic approach, though specific mechanism details are not provided.

items.title: Talazoparib Plus Enzalutamide Before Surgery for Node-Positive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies adding talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard hormone therapy plus enzalutamide before surgery in patients with prostate cancer that has spread to lymph nodes. The study aims to determine if this combination is more effective than standard treatment alone and is currently recruiting.

items.title: Risk-Adapted Treatment for High-Volume Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 study evaluates a personalized treatment approach for newly diagnosed metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer with high tumor burden. Patients receive treatment intensity matched to their risk level, followed by treatment reduction. The study measures survival, quality of life, and sexual function. Enrollment has not yet begun.

items.title: Phase 3: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone vs Standard Care in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial compares overall survival in patients receiving xaluritamig (a novel bispecific antibody) plus abiraterone versus standard chemotherapy or hormone therapy options. The study is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have not yet received chemotherapy. This represents a potentially significant treatment advancement.

items.title: Phase 1 Safety Study of Xaluritamig in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This early-phase trial evaluates the safety profile of xaluritamig, a novel bispecific antibody therapy, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is actively recruiting and aims to establish safe dosing for future larger trials.

items.title: Carboplatin for Metastatic CRPC with DNA Repair Gene Mutations
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial evaluated carboplatin chemotherapy specifically in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers with homologous recombination DNA repair defects. The study aimed to characterize which molecular abnormalities predict response to carboplatin. Results may help identify which patients benefit from platinum chemotherapy.

items.title: Radium-223 With or Without M3814 and Avelumab for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial compares radium-223 (a radiopharmaceutical for bone metastases) alone versus combined with M3814 (a DNA repair inhibitor) or both M3814 and avelumab (immunotherapy) in castration-resistant prostate cancer with bone spread. The study is recruiting and tests whether adding drugs that enhance radiation effects improves outcomes.

items.title: Tinengotinib Combined With Standard Treatments in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates tinengotinib (a novel targeted therapy) combined with either abiraterone or enzalutamide in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if tinengotinib can be safely added to standard hormone therapies to improve their effectiveness.

items.title: Phase 1: Actinium-225-J591 Plus Lutetium-177-PSMA for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This early-phase dose-finding study tests a novel combination of two radioactive treatments targeting prostate cancer cells: actinium-225-J591 and lutetium-177-PSMA. Both deliver radiation directly to cancer cells. The study is recruiting and aims to find the highest safe dose of this dual radiopharmaceutical approach.

items.title: Dual-Target CAR-NK Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates ETB-DualNK-01, an experimental cell therapy using engineered natural killer cells that target both PSMA and PSCA proteins on prostate cancer cells. The study is recruiting patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer to determine safety and early effectiveness of this immunotherapy approach.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 for Metastatic CRPC With Bone Metastases
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial studies the combination of olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) with radium-223 (targeted radiation for bone metastases) in castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is no longer enrolling but continues following participants. It tests whether blocking DNA repair while delivering radiation to bone metastases improves outcomes.

items.title: Phase 1/2 Study of GDC-1261 in Advanced or Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This early-phase trial evaluates the safety, drug levels in blood, and preliminary effectiveness of GDC-1261, a new investigational drug for advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to identify the recommended dose for future studies.

items.title: Multi-Target Radioligand Therapy for Neuroendocrine Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study evaluates targeted radiation treatments for metastatic neuroendocrine prostate cancer, a rare aggressive form. Patients receive radioligand therapy targeting PSMA, SSTR2, or GRPR proteins based on imaging results. The study is no longer enrolling but monitors how tumor targets change after treatment.

items.title: Pocenbrodib With or Without Darolutamide in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1b/2a dose-finding trial evaluates pocenbrodib (a novel BET inhibitor) alone or combined with darolutamide (hormone therapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and tests safety and early anti-tumor activity of this new drug class.

items.title: Phase 3: Adding Docetaxel for Suboptimal Response to Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This large phase 3 trial tests whether adding docetaxel chemotherapy improves outcomes for metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients whose PSA does not drop adequately on standard hormone treatment alone. The study is recruiting and compares chemotherapy addition versus continuing hormone therapy only.

items.title: Phase 3: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide vs Enzalutamide Alone in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat (an investigational epigenetic drug) combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer patients who have not previously received hormone therapy or chemotherapy. The study is recruiting for this potentially practice-changing trial.

items.title: Luxdegalutamide Plus Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates luxdegalutamide (a next-generation androgen receptor blocker) at two different doses combined with lutetium-177-PSMA-617 (Pluvicto, an approved radioligand therapy) versus Pluvicto alone in metastatic CRPC patients previously treated with hormone therapy. The study is no longer enrolling and will determine the best dose combination.

items.title: Phase 3: Lutetium-177-PSMA vs Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares lutetium-177-PSMA-617 (Pluvicto) radioligand therapy versus active monitoring in patients with oligometastatic (limited spread) prostate cancer recurring after initial treatment. The study is recruiting and tests whether early treatment with radioligand therapy can delay disease progression and postpone the need for hormone therapy.

items.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy to Restore Hormone Sensitivity in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests bipolar androgen therapy using testosterone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The treatment cycles between very low and very high testosterone levels to potentially resensitize cancer cells to hormone therapy. The study is recruiting and measures changes in androgen receptor sensitivity.

items.title: Phase 3: Actinium-225-PSMA Plus Hormone Therapy vs Standard Care
items.summary: This major phase 3 trial compares actinium-225-PSMA-617 (a more potent radioligand therapy than lutetium-177) combined with hormone therapy versus standard treatments in metastatic CRPC patients previously treated with one hormone therapy but no chemotherapy. The study is recruiting and tests whether this combination improves progression-free survival.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation, particularly through NFκB and IL-6/JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways, reshapes the biology of advanced prostate cancer. These inflammatory signals interact with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, resistance to treatment, and metastasis through epigenetic changes in cancer cells.

items.title: DNA Vaccine Targeting PSMA Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA that generates strong immune responses against prostate cancer. In animal models, the vaccine prevented tumor growth and lung metastases, and when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy, enhanced anti-tumor immunity by increasing immune activation and reducing immune-suppressing cells.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: Researchers developed a new dual-targeted drug (compound 21d) that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. This approach addresses resistance to AKT inhibitors alone, which often fails due to c-MYC upregulation. The dual inhibitor shows promise in overcoming this treatment resistance mechanism.

items.title: Meta-Analysis: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors Show Limited Benefit in Unselected Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 metastatic CRPC patients found that immune checkpoint inhibitors alone show modest benefits in unselected patients. One-year survival was 63% and two-year survival 39%. However, combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors plus other agents showed better outcomes than single or dual checkpoint blockade alone.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone Health During Enzalutamide Plus Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This phase 2 trial (BonEnza) found that adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening drug) to hormone therapy plus enzalutamide significantly reduced bone density loss in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients. After 18 months, patients receiving zoledronic acid maintained stable bone density while those without it experienced significant bone loss at the hip and spine.
